newsitem.title: ITALY: Paris, Bonn want EMU members accord by Sept - paper.
newsitem.headline: Paris, Bonn want EMU members accord by Sept - paper.

text.p: Germany and France will try to reach a consensus by September this year on which European countries will be able to qualify for a single currency from its 1998 start, Italian newspaper Il Sole 24 Ore said on Thursday.

Il Sole reported on Wednesday a deal was taking shape between Paris and Bonn to keep Italy and Spain out of economic and monetary union (EMU) at its start. Italy, France and Germany quickly dismissed Wednesday's report, denying the existence of any "secret deals" to keep the two countries out.
Il Sole gave no sources for its report on Thursday but said attempts to find an "early accord" had been requested several times by Paris since the start of the year.

It said the idea of bringing forward an informal selection for EMU entry had run into difficulties particularly regarding Italy and Spain, as Germany had assumed an intransigent attitude to these two which Paris had been forced to take notice of in recent weeks.

It said negotiations were still open and caught on one hand between the threat of a delay to EMU on the part of Germany and on the other by the lack of economic data on the state of countries' public finances, with the first reliable figures only likely to be available in August and September.

Il Sole noted the denials from the French and German finance ministries on Wednesday that secret deals existed and said the negotiations were only taking shape now on who joins EMU at its start scheduled for 1999.

"The need to balance German predominance holds the French position open to favouring a guaranteed entry for Italy," the newspaper said but added that now French President Jacques Chirac had to consider Germany's intransigence "in an unequivocal way".

It quoted Bonn sources as saying the differences between Bonn and Paris on selecting countries to take part in EMU "are destined to get closer to each other and even the government and the Bank of France are considering the idea of starting the Euro without a wide number of countries."
